source.title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures

accepted.question_text: For the delayed constant-yield harvesting equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) - h, where h > 0 and the recruitment function f is continuous, decreasing, satisfies f(0) = b > 1, and makes x f(x) increasing and bounded, is the largest persisting set D_h monotone decreasing as the harvesting quota h increases? Equivalently, if h_1 <= h_2, must every initial condition whose solution persists under harvesting level h_2 also persist under harvesting level h_1, so that D_{h_2} is a subset of D_{h_1}?

For the normalized delayed Pielou harvesting equation x_{n+1} = b x_n/(1 + x_{n-1}) - h with b > 1 and 0 < h < 1, are all persistent solutions whose terms are eventually larger than the lower positive equilibrium xbar_{1,h} attracted to the upper positive equilibrium xbar_{2,h}?

For the normalized delayed Pielou harvesting equation x_{n+1} = b x_n/(1 + x_{n-1}) - h with b > 1, let D_h be the largest set of initial conditions whose solutions persist under harvesting quota h. When 0 < h < 1, prove or disprove that the persistent set at quota 1 is contained in the persistent set at quota h, that is, D_1 is a subset of D_h.

For the normalized delayed Pielou harvesting equation x_{n+1} = b x_n/(1 + x_{n-1}) - h with b > 1 and h > 1, characterize the largest persistent set D_h of initial conditions. In particular, determine whether D_h is closed and whether D_h is connected.

For the no-delay p-periodic stocking equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) + h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic sequence of nonnegative stocking quotas with positive total stocking over one period, each quota ordering has a globally attracting p-periodic solution. If xbar_av is the average of the attracting p-periodic solution for one ordering of the stocking quotas and xhat_av is the average for a permutation of the same quotas, how are xbar_av and xhat_av related?

For the Beverton-Holt periodic harvesting equation x_{n+1} = K mu x_n/(K + (mu - 1)x_n) - h_n with K > 0, mu > 1, and a p-periodic sequence h_n of nonnegative harvesting quotas that gives a nonempty persistent set, compare the average of the attracting population cycle for one ordering of the quotas with the average for any permutation of the same quotas. How does xbar_av, the attractor average for h_n, relate to xhat_av, the attractor average for the permuted sequence hhat_n?

For the Beverton-Holt periodic harvesting equation x_{n+1} = K mu x_n/(K + (mu - 1)x_n) - h_n, suppose a fixed p-periodic multiset of harvesting quotas h_0, h_1, ..., h_{p-1} gives a nonempty persistent set. Among all permutations of those quotas, which ordering produces the largest persistent set of initial populations whose trajectories survive indefinitely?
accepted.context_brief: Largest persistent set under quota permutation

accepted.question_text: For the normalized delayed Pielou equation x_{n+1} = b x_n/(1 + x_{n-1}) - h_n, the constant-harvest case h_n = 1 has the invariant I_b(x_n, x_{n-1}) = ((1 + b)/(1 + x_n))((1 + b)/(1 + x_{n-1}))(1 + x_n + x_{n-1}). What becomes of these invariants when the harvesting sequence is perturbed periodically or nonautonomously as h_n = 1 +/- epsilon_n?

For the delayed p-periodic stocking equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) + h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic nonnegative stocking sequence with positive total stocking over one period, a p-periodic solution exists and is known to be globally attracting when p = 2. Is that p-periodic solution globally attracting for every period p > 2?

For the delayed p-periodic harvesting equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) - h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic nonnegative harvesting sequence, investigate the global dynamics: characterize persistence and extinction, the structure of any persistent set, boundedness and strong persistence of persistent solutions, periodic attractors or other limiting behavior, and how these properties depend on the sequence h_0, h_1, ..., h_{p-1}.

trace.notes: Normalized the input as a zbMATH resolver URL. The zbMATH API record 6633387 identified Zbl 1347.92058 and provided the journal PDF link used as the readable primary source.

Mapped the PDF into introduction, constant yield harvesting/stocking, periodic harvesting/stocking, no-delay and one-unit-delay subsections, and identified explicit conjecture and open-problem blocks on pages 241, 242, 244, 246, and 247.
Extracted Conjecture 2.3, Conjecture 2.7, Open Problem 2.1, and Open Problem 2.2 from the one-unit delay constant harvesting discussion.
Extracted Open Problems 3.1 through 3.4 from the no-delay periodic stocking and harvesting discussion.
Extracted Conjecture 3.6 from periodic stocking with one-unit delay and Open Problem 3.5 from periodic harvesting with one-unit delay.
Expanded Conjecture 2.3 by inlining the delayed harvesting equation, assumptions on f, and the meaning of D_h as the largest persisting set.
Expanded Conjecture 2.7 by naming the normalized delayed Pielou equation and specifying the equilibrium-attraction claim.
Expanded Open Problem 2.1 by restating Eq. (2.8), the parameter range 0 < h < 1, and the persistent-set inclusion D_1 subset D_h.
Expanded Open Problem 2.2 by restating Eq. (2.8), the parameter range h > 1, and the requested topological properties of D_h.
Expanded Open Problem 3.1 by inlining the no-delay periodic stocking equation, quota assumptions, attractor-average notation, and permutation comparison.
Expanded Open Problem 3.2 by restating the Beverton-Holt harvesting model and the comparison of attractor averages under quota permutations.
Expanded Open Problem 3.3 by restating the fixed p-periodic quota multiset and the request to identify the permutation with largest persistent set.
Expanded Open Problem 3.4 by inlining the invariant from Eq. (2.9) and the perturbed harvesting form h_n = 1 +/- epsilon_n.
Expanded Conjecture 3.6 by restating the delayed p-periodic stocking equation and known p = 2 global-attraction context.
Expanded Open Problem 3.5 by restating the delayed p-periodic harvesting equation and making the broad dynamics target explicit without adding claims beyond the surrounding setup.

No near-duplicates were merged. Problems about quota-order effects for stocking, harvesting averages, and largest persistent sets were kept separate because they concern different equations or objectives.

Accepted ten items. Each rewritten question is self-contained, avoids source-pointing language, includes solved-status metadata, and is grounded in located source pages. Evidence quotes are intentionally short locator excerpts to keep the returned JSON copyright-compliant.
Saved exact JSON output to outputs/parse-paper/6633387.json and outputs/latest.json.
